result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.union_all()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Combine any number of graphs with union(). twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.union_all()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Combine any number of graphs with union(). title: >- [Graph.union_all()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Combine any number of graphs with union(). page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Combine any number of graphs with `union()`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L40413-L40463){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.union_all(graphs) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Union of many graphs](../assets/graphs/union-all.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three snapshots of contacts among the same four people, nodes 1 to 4: the first has edge 1–2, the second 2–3 (teal), the third 3–4 (violet) and 1–2 again. Edge 1–2 is in two snapshots, so it is ink. union_all merges nodes by id and keeps every edge: the path 1–2–3–4 with 3 edges, each in the color of the snapshot it came from." width="100%"} Applies `union()` from left to right: nodes with the same ID are merged, and every edge of every graph is kept (edges joining the same pair of IDs are merged). Use it to combine several snapshots or layers that share a node numbering into one graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [graphs]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A non-empty list of graphs with the same directedness. None is modified. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph (a copy, if only one graph is given). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the list is empty or the graphs differ in directedness. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Equivalent to `graphs[0].union(graphs[1]).union(graphs[2])...`, so where graphs disagree on a label or attribute, the earlier graph wins as described in `union()`. Mirrors NetworkX's `union_all`, except that NetworkX requires disjoint node sets while EdgeCase merges by ID (use `disjoint_union_all()` to keep graphs apart). ## Examples {.doc-examples} Three snapshots of contacts among the same people, combined: ::: {#ffa98372 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec def snapshot(pairs): g = ec.Graph() for _ in range(4): g.add_node() return g.add_edges(pairs) days = [snapshot([(1, 2)]), snapshot([(2, 3)]), snapshot([(3, 4), (1, 2)])] ec.Graph.union_all(days).count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: :::
